questions.question_text: At simple interest, the interest earned in 3 years is 3/10 of the principal. What is the ratio of the amount after 8 years to the amount after 2 years?
questions.explanation: Annual rate=10%; amounts are 1.8P and 1.2P; ratio=3:2.

questions.question_text: Two sums differ by Rs 1,000 and are lent at 8% and 10% simple interest respectively for 4 years. The larger sum is at the lower rate. If the interest difference is Rs 800, find the smaller sum.
questions.explanation: Let larger=x and smaller=x-1,000. Difference=.4(x-1,000)-.32x=800; x=15,000; smaller=Rs14,000.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question; independently calculated; concept reference: NCERT Class VIII Mathematics, Comparing Quantities; scope reference: SSC CGL Quantitative Aptitude syllabus

questions.question_text: A sum earns Rs 4,500 at 7.5% simple interest. If the rate had been 2.5 percentage points lower and time 4 years longer, the interest would be unchanged. The original time was 8 years. Find the principal.
questions.explanation: For original 7.5%x8=.60P; alternative 5%(8+4)=.60P, so conditions match; P=4,500/.60=Rs7,500.

questions.question_text: At simple interest, a sum becomes 7/5 of itself in 8 years. How many years will it take to become 13/5 of itself at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Eight-year interest=2P/5; to reach 13P/5 requires interest 8P/5, four times as much, so 32 years.
